From 7a58b8d6021426b796eebfae80983374d9a80a75 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Date: Sun, 18 Sep 2022 11:33:12 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] usb: chipidea: fix deadlock in ci_otg_del_timer

There is a deadlock in ci_otg_del_timer(), the process is
shown below:

    (thread 1)                  |        (thread 2)
ci_otg_del_timer()              | ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
  ...                           |
  spin_lock_irqsave() //(1)     |  ...
  ...                           |
  hrtimer_cancel()              |  spin_lock_irqsave() //(2)
  (block forever)

We hold ci->lock in position (1) and use hrtimer_cancel() to
wait ci_otg_hrtimer_func() to stop, but ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
also need ci->lock in position (2). As a result, the
hrtimer_cancel() in ci_otg_del_timer() will be blocked forever.

This patch extracts hrtimer_cancel() from the protection of
spin_lock_irqsave() in order that the ci_otg_hrtimer_func()
could obtain the ci->lock.

What`s more, there will be no race happen. Because the
"next_timer" is always under the protection of
spin_lock_irqsave() and we only check whether "next_timer"
equals to NUM_OTG_FSM_TIMERS in the following code.

Fixes: 3a316ec4c91c ("usb: chipidea: use hrtimer for otg fsm timers")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220918033312.94348-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c b/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
index ada78daba6df..c17516c29b63 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c
@@ -256,8 +256,10 @@ static void ci_otg_del_timer(struct ci_hdrc *ci, enum otg_fsm_timer t)
 	ci->enabled_otg_timer_bits &= ~(1 << t);
 	if (ci->next_otg_timer == t) {
 		if (ci->enabled_otg_timer_bits == 0) {
+			spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ci->lock, flags);
 			/* No enabled timers after delete it */
 			hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer);
+			spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags);
 			ci->next_otg_timer = NUM_OTG_FSM_TIMERS;
 		} else {
 			/* Find the next timer */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/usb/chipidea/otg_fsm.c`**
- In the function `ci_otg_del_timer`, the sequence of operations has been modified to prevent a deadlock.
- The `hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer);` call has been moved outside of the `spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags);` block. 
- After checking if there are no enabled timers, the lock is released with `spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ci->lock, flags);` before calling `hrtimer_cancel()`.
- After the timer is canceled, the lock is reacquired with `spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags);` before updating `ci->next_otg_timer`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The changes address a deadlock situation where two threads could block each other while trying to acquire the same lock. By moving the `hrtimer_cancel()` call outside of the lock, the function allows `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()` to acquire the lock without being blocked, thus preventing the deadlock.
- The modification ensures that the critical section where `next_timer` is checked remains protected by the lock, maintaining thread safety while avoiding race conditions. This restructuring of the code allows for proper synchronization between the timer cancellation and the lock management.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags); //(1)
hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer); 
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags); //(2)
```
Reason:
The deadlock occurs because `ci_otg_del_timer()` acquires `ci->lock` (1) and then calls `hrtimer_cancel()`, which requires `ci->lock` to be held by `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()`. If `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()` is invoked while `ci_otg_del_timer()` is holding the lock, it will attempt to acquire the same lock (2), leading to a situation where both functions are waiting on each other indefinitely.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ci->lock, flags);
hrtimer_cancel(&ci->otg_fsm_hrtimer);
spin_lock_irqsave(&ci->lock, flags);
```
Reason:
The patch fixes the deadlock by unlocking `ci->lock` before calling `hrtimer_cancel()`, allowing `ci_otg_hrtimer_func()` to acquire the lock if it needs to. This change ensures that `hrtimer_cancel()` can execute without being blocked by the lock held by `ci_otg_del_timer()`, thus preventing the deadlock situation.
